newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares ease on profit-taking, seen weaker.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares ease on profit-taking, seen weaker.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged down on Western profit-taking on Friday and traders forecast a further fall over the next few days.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares fell 0.83 percent to 191.23 on $22.65 million in volume.
"The West is selling in big lots," said Andrei Ippolitov, corporate securities director at IK Prospekt.
Andrei Galperin, a trader from Creditanstalt-Grant, said the market should continue to ease in the next few days.
"The market is stagnating," he said, adding that some investors would take profits on what they considered over-valued shares.
Some less liquid shares in utilities, telecommunications and oil have soared over the last few weeks on relatively small buy orders.

Ippolitov said a parliamentary resolution on Friday asking President Boris Yeltsin to temporarily relieve Kremlin chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais of his duties because of his alleged role in a political scandal had pressured the market.
The Duma also urged Yeltsin to relieve first deputy prime minister Viktor Ilyushin, a former presidential adviser, of his duties temporarily. Ilyushin and Chubais deny any wrongdoing.
But Ippolitov said the market was not affected by Finance Minister Alexander Livshits comments that talks with the IMF would lead to eventual payment of delayed tranches of a $10 billion loan.
"People who believe that we will not get the the tranche left Russia a long time ago," Ippolitov said.
Mosenergo edged up to $0.997 from $0.996 at Thursday's close on healthy reports about the company's profits in 1995, Ippolitov said.
The company said 1995 sales rose to $2.93 billion from $1.93 billion in 1994 to U.S. accounting standards. Its net profit was $383 million after $129 million in 1994.
Red October rose to $19.00 from $17.75 at Thursday's close, UES was $0.0826 after $0.0830, Norilsk Nickel fell to $6.00 from $6.10 and Rostelekom rose to $2.45 after $2.25.
